rv.q: But it's bloated: too many subplots that don't amount to anything, and no way it has to drone on for over two and a half hours.
Funny without being frivolous, political without becoming didactic, and deeply compassionate without ever surrendering its bite, Wasserstein’s writing still lands.
Like frosted tips and dial-up internet, An American Daughter emerges as another relic of the ’90s best consigned to that bygone era.

cn.t: Wasserstein's political drama about women in power remains disturbingly relevant, though critics find the play itself disappointing despite intermittent charms and an elaborate production.
